title: Sky mandates paid maintenance of external accessibility channels while budgeting 0 USDS per month for it
content:
Two provisions in the same Article point in opposite directions.

- **A.5.2.1.1 (External Platforms):** Sky *must* support accessibility by **paying** Ecosystem Actors to maintain accounts and channels on external platforms such as Twitter and Telegram.
- **A.5.2.1.3.1 (Amount):** the Accessibility communication channel budget is **0 USDS per month**, implemented with DssVest, recurring monthly.

A funding-dependent obligation is live while its funding line is explicitly zero. Both readings are defensible — the mandate may be aspirational pending a budget request, or the channels may be maintained from another budget. The text does not say which.

The structural point is that a zero-amount recurring budget is not the same as an absent one: the line exists, is implemented with DssVest, and can be raised without amending the obligation. That makes 0 a deliberate placeholder rather than an omission, but it leaves the 'must pay' unenforceable meanwhile.
description: A.5.2.1.1 requires paying Ecosystem Actors to run external platform accounts; A.5.2.1.3.1 sets that recurring DssVest budget to 0 USDS — the obligation stands with no funding attached.
